public import FormalConjecturesUtil


/-!
# Erdős Problem 946

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/946](https://www.erdosproblems.com/946)
 - [ErMi52] Erdős, P. and Mirsky, L., The distribution of values of the divisor function {$d(n)$}.
   Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) (1952), 257--271.
 - [Sp81] Spiro, C. A., The frequency with which an integral-valued, prime-independent,
   multiplicative or additive function of n divides a polynomial function of n.
 - [He84] Heath-Brown, D. R., The divisor function at consecutive integers.
   Mathematika 31 (1984), no. 2, 141--149.
 - [Hi85] Hildebrand, A., The divisor function at consecutive integers. Pacific J. Math.
   (1987), 307--319
 - [EPS87] Erdős, P., Pomerance, C., and Sarkőzy, A., On locally repeated values of
   arithmetic functions. III. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1987), 1--7.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Real
open scoped ArithmeticFunction.sigma

namespace Erdos946

/--
There are infinitely many $n$ such that $τ(n) = τ(n+1)$. Proved in [He84].
Here τ is the divisor counting function, which is `σ 0` in mathlib.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos946.lean#L75"]
theorem erdos_946 : {n : ℕ | σ 0 n = σ 0 (n + 1)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
There are infinitely many $n$ such that $τ(n) = τ(n + 5040)$. Proved in [Sp81].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_946.variants.spiro_5040 : {n : ℕ | σ 0 n = σ 0 (n + 5040)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/-- Number of $n \le x$ with $τ(n) = τ(n+1)$. -/
noncomputable def erdos946Count (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ((Finset.range (⌊x⌋₊ + 1)).filter (fun n => σ 0 n = σ 0 (n + 1))).card

/--
The number of $n \le x$ with $τ(n) = τ(n+1)$ is at least $x / (\log x)^7$ for all sufficiently
large $x$. Proved in [He84].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_946.variants.heathbrown_lower_bound :
    (fun x => x / (x.log)^7) =O[atTop] erdos946Count := by
  sorry

/--
Improved lower bound in [Hi85]: $Ω(x / (\log \log x)^3)$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_946.variants.hildebrand_lower_bound :
    (fun x => x / (x.log.log)^3) =O[atTop] erdos946Count := by
  sorry

/--
Upper bound in [EPS87]: $O(x / \sqrt{\log \log x})$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_946.variants.upper_bound : erdos946Count =O[atTop] (fun x => x / √x.log.log ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos946

findings.description: The docstring says the count "is at least $x / (\log x)^7$ for all sufficiently large $x$", which has an implied constant of 1. The Lean statement `(fun x => x / (x.log)^7) =O[atTop] erdos946Count` only asserts that erdos946Count x ≥ c·x/(log x)^7 eventually, for some constant c > 0. That is the Vinogradov ≫ which Heath-Brown proved and the source quotes. The Lean is correct; the docstring overstates the theorem it attributes to [He84] by dropping the constant.
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/946: "More generally, he showed that the number of such $n\leq x$ is $\gg \frac{x}{(\log x)^7}$." Hildebrand, Pacific J. Math. 129 (1987), eq. (1.1): "#{n ≤ x: d(n) = d(n+1)} ≫ x(log x)^{-7}". Heath-Brown's zbMATH review of EPS III (Zbl 0631.10029) says "at least of order x(log x)^{-7}".
findings.suggested_fix: Docstring: "The number of $n \le x$ with $τ(n) = τ(n+1)$ is $\gg x / (\log x)^7$, i.e. at least $c\,x/(\log x)^7$ for some constant $c > 0$ and all sufficiently large $x$. Proved in [He84]." The Lean needs no change.

findings.description: Bibliographic slips in the module docstring's reference list; the mathematics is unaffected. (1) [He84] is given as "Mathematika 31 (1984), no. 2, 141--149", but the paper is in issue 1 (June 1984). (2) Hildebrand's paper has the key [Hi85], used both in the reference list and in the `hildebrand_lower_bound` docstring. It was published in 1987 (Pacific J. Math. 129, no. 2; received 1986), and erdosproblems.com cites it as [Hi87]. (3) The [EPS87] title leaves out "certain": the actual title is "On locally repeated values of certain arithmetic functions. III", Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 101 (1987), 1–7.
findings.source_evidence: Crossref, DOI 10.1112/S0025579300010743: Mathematika vol. 31, issue "1", published June 1984, pp. 141-149. Crossref, DOI 10.2140/pjm.1987.129.307: Pacific J. Math. 129, issue 2, 1987, pp. 307-319; the msp.org PDF says "Received March 18, 1986". The erdosproblems.com/946 bibliography key is [Hi87]. Crossref/zbMATH give the title "On locally repeated values of certain arithmetic functions. III", Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 101, 1-7 (1987).
findings.suggested_fix: Change "Mathematika 31 (1984), no. 2" to "no. 1". Rename [Hi85] to [Hi87] in the module docstring and in the `hildebrand_lower_bound` docstring, and add the volume (Pacific J. Math. 129 (1987), no. 2). Change the EPS87 title to "On locally repeated values of certain arithmetic functions. III. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 101 (1987), 1--7."

reformulations.difference: The source asks a yes/no question ("Are there infinitely many n such that τ(n)=τ(n+1)?"). The Lean asserts the affirmative, `{n : ℕ | σ 0 n = σ 0 (n + 1)}.Infinite`, with no `answer(True) ↔` wrapper, as CONTRIBUTING prefers for solved questions. Also, n ranges over ℕ including 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The source records the problem as "PROVED: solved in the affirmative" (Heath-Brown 1984), so asserting P is the same claim as `answer(True) ↔ P`. The n = 0 case is harmless: σ 0 0 = 0 ≠ 1 = σ 0 1, so 0 is never in the set, and the set equals {n | 0 < n ∧ σ 0 n = σ 0 (n+1)}. I proved this set equality in Lean. The linked formal proof (plby/lean-proofs L75) states the same theorem verbatim.

reformulations.difference: The source's lower bound "count ≫ x/(log x)^7" is written as `(fun x => x / (x.log)^7) =O[atTop] erdos946Count`: the bound function is on the left of `=O` and the count on the right. A reader might suspect the sides are swapped, as happened in Erdős 394.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: I proved in Lean that for any f : ℝ → ℝ, `f =O[atTop] erdos946Count ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ x in atTop, c * |f x| ≤ erdos946Count x`. This uses `isBigO_iff'` and the nonnegativity of the count. The right-hand side is exactly the Vinogradov statement count ≫ f. `erdos946Count x` counts n ∈ {0,…,⌊x⌋₊} with τ(n)=τ(n+1), which for x ≥ 0 is #{1 ≤ n ≤ x}, since n = 0 never qualifies.

reformulations.difference: Hildebrand's "count ≫ x/(log log x)^3" is written as `(fun x => x / (x.log.log)^3) =O[atTop] erdos946Count`, with the bound function on the left of `=O`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This is the same lemma as for heathbrown_lower_bound, proved in Lean for arbitrary f: `f =O[atTop] erdos946Count ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ x in atTop, c * |f x| ≤ erdos946Count x`. This is Hildebrand's Theorem 1 ("for sufficiently large x, #{n ≤ x: d(n)=d(n+1)} ≫ x(log log x)^{-3}"). `x.log.log ^ 3` parses as `(log (log x))^3`, which I checked with #check.

review.notes:
I found no misformalization. All five theorems and the helper `erdos946Count` state what erdosproblems.com/946 and the primary literature say:
- erdos_946: τ(n)=τ(n+1) infinitely often (Heath-Brown 1984).
- spiro_5040: τ(n)=τ(n+5040) infinitely often (Spiro 1981; confirmed by Hildebrand's introduction, \"with a = 5040, d(n) = d(n+a) holds for infinitely many integers n\").
- heathbrown_lower_bound: count ≫ x/(log x)^7.
- hildebrand_lower_bound: count ≫ x/(log log x)^3 (Hildebrand's abstract and Theorem 1).
- upper_bound: count ≪ x/√(log log x) (EPS III, Proc. AMS 101 (1987); confirmed by Hildebrand's eq. (1.3) and Heath-Brown's zbMATH review).

Lean checks in /workspace/review:
- σ 0 = #divisors (`sigma_zero_apply`); σ 0 0 = 0.
- `√x.log.log` elaborates to `√(log (log x))`, and `x / (x.log)^7` to `x / (log x)^7`.
- The first solutions are [2, 14, 21, 26, 33, 34, 38], matching OEIS A005237.
- erdos946Count 14 = 2, erdos946Count 13.5 = 1, and erdos946Count x = 0 for x < 0 (all proved).
- The IsBigO encodings are equivalent to ≫ and ≪ (lemma proved).

Status: every declaration is `research solved`, matching the source's PROVED. The `formal_proof` link (plby/lean-proofs @8822f7d, L75) states `Set.Infinite {n : ℕ | σ 0 n = σ 0 (n + 1)}` verbatim. I did not build that external proof. The teorth database lists 946's formal_status as \"unformalized\", which is probably just out of date and does not contradict the file.

The source's other items are not formalized: the longest run of equal-τ integers, Pinner's τ(n)=τ(n+k) for every k ≥ 1, and the conjectured asymptotic c·x/√(log log x) (Tao–Teräväinen, almost all x). These are omissions, not defects.

I could not read HB84's and EPS III's own texts (paywalled or scanned without a text layer). Their results are confirmed by Hildebrand's paper and by Heath-Brown's zbMATH review.

The only findings are two low-stakes minor items: the Heath-Brown docstring drops the implied constant, and there are bibliographic slips in the module docstring.
